name: Mutton Rogan Josh

ingredients.item: whole spices (bay leaf, cinnamon, cloves, cardamom)

steps: Heat mustard oil in a heavy pot until smoking, then let it cool slightly to reduce its pungency.
Add whole spices and asafoetida, and let them sizzle for a few seconds.
Add mutton pieces and sear on high heat until browned on all sides, about 8-10 minutes.
Lower the heat, add kashmiri chilli powder mixed with a little water to prevent burning, and mix well.
Whisk in yogurt gradually while stirring continuously to prevent it from splitting.
Add fennel powder, ginger powder and salt, then add enough water to just cover the mutton.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 40-45 minutes, or pressure cook for 20-25 minutes, until the mutton is completely tender and the oil floats on top.
Simmer uncovered for a final few minutes to adjust the gravy consistency, then serve hot with steamed rice or naan.
tips: Kashmiri chilli powder gives the signature deep red colour without excessive heat; don't substitute with regular hot chilli powder in the same quantity.

name: Chicken Korma
steps: Deep fry sliced onions until deep golden and crisp, then cool and grind into a smooth paste with a little water.
Heat ghee in a pot, add whole spices and let them sizzle for a few seconds.
Add ginger garlic paste and cook briefly, then add the fried onion paste and cashew paste.
Cook the mixture on medium heat for 5-6 minutes, stirring frequently.
Add chicken pieces and salt, and mix well to coat evenly.
Lower the heat and whisk in yogurt gradually, stirring continuously to prevent curdling.
Cover and simmer for 20-25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the chicken is fully cooked and the gravy is thick and creamy.
Serve hot with naan, roti or pulao.
tips: Frying the onions to a deep golden colour before grinding is what gives korma its characteristic richness and colour.

name: Shahi Tukda
steps: Simmer milk in a heavy pot on low heat, stirring frequently and scraping the sides, until it reduces to about a third of its volume and thickens into rabri, about 40-45 minutes; add half the sugar, saffron and cardamom powder partway through.
Meanwhile, trim the crusts off the bread slices and cut each into triangles or rounds.
Prepare a light sugar syrup with the remaining sugar and a little water, heated until slightly sticky.
Heat ghee in a pan and shallow fry the bread pieces until golden and crisp on both sides.
Dip the fried bread briefly into the warm sugar syrup so it soaks in slightly without becoming soggy.
Arrange the syrup-coated bread pieces on a serving plate.
Pour the thickened rabri generously over the bread.
Garnish with chopped nuts and a few saffron strands, and serve warm or chilled.
tips: Keep stirring the milk regularly while reducing it, as it can scorch easily on the bottom of the pot.

name: Mutton Biryani (Mughlai Style)
steps: Marinate mutton with yogurt, half the fried onions, ginger garlic paste, red chilli powder and salt for at least 1-2 hours.
Cook the marinated mutton in a heavy pot with a little water, covered, until nearly tender, about 30-35 minutes on the stovetop or 15-18 minutes under pressure.
Separately, boil the soaked rice in salted water with whole garam masala until about 70% cooked, then drain.
In a heavy-bottomed pot, spread half the mutton with its gravy as the base layer.
Layer half the partially cooked rice on top, then repeat with the remaining mutton and rice.
Sprinkle the remaining fried onions, mint, coriander, saffron milk and a drizzle of ghee over the top layer.
Cover tightly with a lid, sealing the edges with dough if needed, and cook on very low heat (dum) for 25-30 minutes.
Let it rest for 10 minutes off the heat, then gently mix and serve hot with raita.
tips: Sealing the pot tightly for the dum step is essential to trap the steam and fully cook the rice with the mutton's flavour.

name: Sheekh Kebab

ingredients.item: onion, finely chopped and squeezed dry

steps: Combine minced meat with squeezed onion, ginger garlic paste, green chillies, roasted gram flour, garam masala, herbs and salt.
Knead the mixture well by hand for several minutes until it becomes smooth and slightly sticky, which helps it bind on the skewers.
Cover and refrigerate the mixture for at least 30 minutes to firm up.
Wet your hands, take a portion of the mixture, and mould it firmly around a skewer into a long sausage shape.
Preheat a grill, tandoor or oven to high heat.
Cook the kebabs, turning occasionally and brushing with a little oil or ghee, until browned and cooked through, about 15-18 minutes.
Rest briefly before sliding off the skewers.
Serve hot with mint chutney, lemon wedges and sliced onions.
tips: Kneading the mince mixture thoroughly develops a slight stickiness that keeps the kebabs from falling apart while cooking.

name: Murgh Musallam
steps: Clean the whole chicken and make deep slits all over so the marinade penetrates well.
Marinate the chicken with yogurt, ginger garlic paste, half the fried onion paste and salt, and refrigerate for at least 2 hours.
Stuff the cavity of the chicken with boiled eggs and truss it securely with kitchen string to hold its shape.
Heat ghee in a large heavy pot, add whole garam masala, and sear the chicken on all sides until lightly browned.
Add remaining fried onion paste and cashew paste, and cook for a few minutes around the chicken.
Add a little water, cover tightly, and cook on low heat, turning the chicken occasionally, for 40-45 minutes until fully cooked through.
Once tender, uncover and simmer to thicken the gravy to a rich, coating consistency.
Carefully transfer the whole chicken to a serving platter, slice, and spoon the gravy over the top to serve.
tips: Turning the whole chicken gently and occasionally while it cooks ensures even cooking without tearing the skin.

name: Nihari
steps: Heat ghee in a large heavy pot and saute ginger garlic paste until fragrant.
Add the meat and sear on high heat until browned on all sides.
Add nihari masala and salt, and mix well to coat the meat evenly.
Add enough hot water to generously cover the meat, bring to a boil, then reduce to a very low simmer.
Cover and cook on low heat for 3-4 hours, or until the meat is falling-off-the-bone tender, checking occasionally and topping up water if needed.
Mix wheat flour with a little water into a smooth slurry and stir it into the stew to thicken the gravy.
Simmer for another 15-20 minutes until the gravy reaches a thick, glossy consistency.
Garnish with fried onions, julienned ginger, chopped coriander and green chillies, and serve hot with naan or khameeri roti.
tips: Traditionally cooked overnight on very low heat, nihari rewards patience; do not rush the long simmering time.

name: Mughlai Paratha
steps: Knead flour with a little oil, salt and water into a soft dough, cover, and rest for 20-30 minutes.
Divide the dough into balls and roll each into a thin, large round.
Whisk together eggs, chopped onion, green chillies and a pinch of salt in a bowl, then mix in the cooked minced meat.
Heat a griddle and place the rolled dough on it, cooking briefly until it just starts to set.
Pour a portion of the egg-mince mixture onto the centre of the paratha and spread slightly.
Fold the edges of the paratha inward over the filling to form a square packet, sealing it in.
Drizzle oil around the edges and shallow fry on both sides until golden brown and the egg inside is fully cooked, pressing gently with a spatula.
Cut into pieces and serve hot with a squeeze of lime and salad.
tips: Folding the paratha into a tight packet before frying keeps the runny egg filling from leaking out.

name: Shami Kebab
steps: Cook minced mutton and soaked chana dal together with whole spices, ginger garlic paste, salt and just enough water to cover, until both are tender and the water has evaporated, about 25-30 minutes.
Remove the whole spices, cool the mixture slightly, and grind it into a smooth, thick paste using a food processor.
Mix in the beaten egg to bind the mixture, adjusting with a little roasted gram flour if it feels too soft.
Divide the mixture into balls and flatten each into a small, round patty.
Place a little chopped onion and mint in the centre of a patty, fold it over, and seal to encase the stuffing, then flatten again gently.
Heat a shallow layer of oil or ghee in a pan on medium heat.
Shallow fry the patties until golden brown and crisp on both sides, about 3-4 minutes per side.
Serve hot with mint chutney and sliced onions.
tips: Grinding the meat and dal into a very smooth paste is key to the classic melt-in-the-mouth texture of shami kebab.

name: Navratan Korma
steps: Steam or boil the mixed vegetables separately until just tender, keeping them slightly firm.
Heat ghee in a pan and add fried onion paste and cashew paste, cooking for 3-4 minutes.
Lower the heat and whisk in yogurt gradually, stirring continuously.
Add a little water to adjust consistency and bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the cooked vegetables, paneer cubes and pineapple chunks, and mix gently.
Simmer for 8-10 minutes so the flavours meld without overcooking the vegetables.
Adjust salt and add a touch of sugar if desired to balance the sweetness from the pineapple.
Garnish with fried nuts and raisins, and serve hot with naan or pulao.
tips: Cook the vegetables separately and add them near the end so each retains its distinct texture rather than turning mushy.

name: Mutton Kofta Curry
steps: Mix minced mutton with grated onion, half the ginger garlic paste, roasted gram flour and salt into a smooth mixture.
Shape the mixture into small, even-sized balls (koftas) and set aside on a plate.
Bring a pot of lightly salted water to a gentle simmer and poach the koftas for 8-10 minutes until just cooked through; drain and set aside.
Heat ghee in a separate pan, add remaining ginger garlic paste, and prepare a rich onion-tomato-cashew based gravy as used for korma.
Once the gravy base is cooked and the oil separates, whisk in yogurt gradually while stirring.
Add a little water to adjust the gravy consistency and bring to a simmer.
Gently slide the poached koftas into the gravy and simmer for 10-12 minutes so they absorb the flavours without breaking apart.
Garnish with coriander and serve hot with naan or rice.
tips: Poaching the koftas in water first, rather than frying, keeps them tender and prevents the gravy from becoming greasy.

name: Chicken Chaap
steps: Marinate chicken pieces with yogurt, raw papaya paste, ginger garlic paste and salt, and refrigerate for at least 1 hour to tenderize.
Heat ghee in a heavy pan, add whole spices and let them sizzle for a few seconds.
Add the marinated chicken along with the marinade and cook on medium heat, stirring occasionally, for 10 minutes.
Add fried onion paste and a little water, then cover and simmer on low heat for 15-20 minutes until the chicken is tender.
Uncover and simmer to reduce the gravy to a thick, clinging consistency that coats the chicken.
Adjust salt and finish with a drizzle of ghee.
Garnish with fried onions and serve hot with paratha or roomali roti.
tips: Raw papaya paste acts as a natural tenderizer, giving the chicken a very soft texture typical of this dish.

name: Galouti Kebab

ingredients.item: galouti spice blend (mace, nutmeg, cardamom, etc.)

steps: Combine the finely ground mince with raw papaya paste, ginger garlic paste, galouti spice blend, fried onion paste and salt.
Knead the mixture thoroughly for several minutes until it becomes very smooth and cohesive.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour, or ideally longer, to let the papaya tenderize the meat.
Just before cooking, mix in roasted gram flour to help bind the delicate mixture.
Shape small portions into thin, flat, round patties directly in your palm, handling gently as the mixture is soft.
Heat a generous amount of ghee in a flat pan on medium heat.
Carefully place the patties in the pan and shallow fry until golden brown and cooked through, about 2-3 minutes per side, turning very gently.
Serve immediately, hot, with warm roomali roti or ulte tawa ka paratha.
tips: The mince must be ground extremely fine, almost paste-like, for the characteristic melt-in-the-mouth texture.

name: Badam Halwa
steps: Soak almonds in hot water for at least 4-6 hours, or overnight, then peel off the skins.
Grind the peeled almonds with milk into a smooth, thick paste.
Heat ghee in a heavy pan and add the almond paste, stirring continuously on low-medium heat.
Cook the paste, stirring constantly, for about 15-20 minutes until it darkens slightly and starts releasing ghee at the edges.
Add sugar and continue stirring; the mixture will loosen as the sugar dissolves and then gradually thicken again.
Add saffron strands and cardamom powder, and keep stirring until the halwa turns glossy and starts leaving the sides of the pan.
Cook for a final few minutes until the desired thick, fudge-like consistency is reached.
Serve warm, garnished with slivered almonds.
tips: Continuous stirring on low-medium heat prevents the almond paste from scorching, which happens easily due to its high fat content.

name: Shahi Paneer Korma
steps: Heat ghee in a pan, add whole spices and let them sizzle for a few seconds.
Add ginger garlic paste and cook briefly, then add fried onion paste and the cashew-melon seed paste.
Cook the mixture on medium heat for 5-6 minutes, stirring frequently to avoid sticking.
Lower the heat and whisk in yogurt gradually, stirring continuously.
Add a little water to adjust consistency and bring the gravy to a gentle simmer.
Add paneer cubes and simmer for 5-6 minutes so they soak up the flavours.
Adjust salt, finish with a drizzle of ghee, and simmer for a final minute.
Serve hot garnished with slivered nuts, alongside naan or sheermal.
tips: Keep the flame gentle after adding yogurt to maintain a smooth, unsplit gravy.

name: Keema Matar
steps: Heat oil in a pan and saute chopped onion until golden brown.
Add ginger garlic paste and cook for a minute, then add chopped tomatoes.
Cook until the tomatoes soften and the oil separates from the masala, about 8 minutes.
Add chilli powder and the minced meat, breaking up any lumps with the back of a spoon.
Cook on medium-high heat, stirring frequently, until the mince is browned and releases its juices, about 8-10 minutes.
Add green peas, salt and a little water, then cover and simmer for 15-18 minutes until the mince and peas are fully cooked.
Sprinkle garam masala on top, mix well, and simmer for a final 2 minutes.
Garnish with coriander and serve hot with roti or pulao.
tips: Breaking the mince apart thoroughly while browning it prevents large clumps and ensures even cooking.

name: Mutton Korma

ingredients.item: whole spices (bay leaf, cinnamon, cloves, cardamom)

steps: Heat ghee in a heavy pot, add whole spices and let them sizzle.
Add ginger garlic paste and cook briefly, then add mutton pieces and sear on high heat until browned.
Add fried onion paste and poppy seed-cashew paste, and cook for 5-6 minutes, stirring frequently.
Lower the heat and whisk in yogurt gradually, stirring continuously to prevent curdling.
Add salt and enough water to just cover the mutton.
Cover and cook on low heat, or pressure cook, until the mutton is completely tender, about 40-45 minutes on stovetop or 20-22 minutes under pressure.
Once tender, simmer uncovered to thicken the gravy to a rich, creamy consistency.
Serve hot with naan, sheermal or steamed rice.
tips: Poppy seed paste adds body and a subtle nutty depth typical of Mughlai kormas; toast the poppy seeds lightly before grinding for extra flavour.

name: Firni
steps: Soak rice for 30 minutes, then drain and coarsely grind it, either in a blender pulsed briefly or with a mortar and pestle.
Bring milk to a boil in a heavy pot, then reduce heat to a gentle simmer.
Slowly add the coarsely ground rice while stirring continuously to prevent lumps.
Simmer on low heat, stirring frequently, for 15-18 minutes until the rice is cooked and the mixture thickens to a custard-like consistency.
Add sugar, cardamom powder and saffron strands, and continue cooking for another 5 minutes.
Remove from heat and let the mixture cool slightly.
Pour into individual earthen or ceramic bowls and refrigerate for at least 2 hours to set and chill.
Garnish with chopped nuts before serving cold.
tips: Traditionally set in clay pots (matkas), which help absorb excess moisture and lend a subtle earthy aroma.

name: Zarda (Sweet Saffron Rice)

ingredients.item: saffron strands, soaked in warm milk

steps: Boil the soaked rice in plenty of water with whole spices until about 80% cooked, then drain well and set aside.
Heat ghee in a heavy pot and fry the mixed nuts and raisins until golden; remove and set aside.
In the same pot, prepare a sugar syrup by dissolving sugar in a little water and simmering until slightly sticky.
Add the saffron milk and food colour, if using, to the syrup and mix well.
Gently fold in the partially cooked rice, taking care not to break the grains.
Cover and cook on very low heat for 12-15 minutes, allowing the rice to absorb the syrup and finish cooking through steam.
Gently fold in the fried nuts and raisins.
Serve warm or at room temperature as a festive sweet.
tips: Handle the rice gently once the syrup is added, using a light folding motion instead of vigorous stirring to keep the grains intact.
